# NOTES

## BOOK 1 of 2: THE O'RUDDY (Stephen Crane & Robert Barr, 1903)

**Narrator:** Tom O'Ruddy, 18 at father's death. Family seat Glandore, near Old Head of Kinsale, Co. Cork. Estate steward Mickey Clancy; priest Father Donovan. Father (d. ~1 month before story) was a soldier with King Louis's French army.

**Father's bequest:** two swords (grand one from King Louis; plain one), last cask of brandy, papers belonging to young Lord Strepp (now Earl of Westport, London). Father lent Strepp a pair of breeches in France. Advice: "never be civil to a king's officer"; "wherever you see a red coat... there is a rogue." Ship "Martha Bixby." Father: "I am glad I had you taught to read."

**Ch I (Bristol):** Cove of Cork → Bristol. Inn; little fat landlord. Supper room: garrulous man in plum-colour; Lord Strepp (~20, fair unpowdered hair); Colonel Royale (~40, clear-eyed, = Clarence Royale); Forister (dark-skinned, proud, = Reginald Forister, Earl's shipping partner). Story: Strepp's father hung breeches on bush after fording stream; "blackguard wild Irishman" stole papers. O'Ruddy: "That, sir, is a lie." Gives lie twice. Waiters bundle him out. Strepp visits: duel at daybreak. O'Ruddy lies that his friend will be present. Forister in hall mocks Irish ("naked... clubs"); O'Ruddy boxes his ear and kicks him through front door into yard. Lands on upper servant with cloaks. Earl of Westport (tall, "like an old eagle", black cloak) with two ladies; one pair of "bright liquid eyes" (Lady Mary). Earl: "Come to my chamber in the morning, O'Ruddy." Colonel and Strepp seen laughing over railing.

**Ch II:** Irish keening vagrant, red-haired **Paddy** (bedraggled, blue eyes). O'Ruddy dresses him in blue velvet, flowered waistcoat, pink stockings, cocked hat; father's King Louis sword hung on string round Paddy's neck. Coaching: "bow for your life." Field: Paddy's "lashings" (wager of meat/drink). O'Ruddy fences; laughs in Colonel's face; Colonel furious; O'Ruddy pricks him four times (sword arm). Strepp stops: "Enough." Colonel sobs "I couldn't reach him." Crowd of Bristol boys. O'Ruddy: "Well, I won't kill him... Damme if I will!" Paddy struts as "King of Ireland"; O'Ruddy slaps him.

**Ch III:** Papers missing; Paddy had them (boots joke: "one is badly worn at the heel"). O'Ruddy suspects Forister. Landlord: Forister gone to Bath. Highwayman **Jem Bottles** (ballads: 7 in Bristol, 3 in Bath; mother; cheese; snuff-boxes; sheep-stealer turned highwayman after stealing Farmer Hants's eggs from Little Susan). O'Ruddy beats him with pistol. Jem's stable: three horses behind mother's cottage. Mother = **Dame Bottles** (sensible, scolds). Jem takes 14 guineas; O'Ruddy has 1. Ride to Bath.

**Ch IV:** O'Ruddy dreams of Lady Mary ("eyes put in chains"). Bath: Forister gone back to Bristol. Roadside inn near Bristol: Jem's chambermaid sweetheart. Paddy has trapped small black man (Forister) in room; threatens to "slice your heart into pieces of paper."

**Ch V:** Forister: "king of the Irelands," "red-headed duke." Denies papers; threatens to kill O'Ruddy in Bristol. Paddy's horse-lifting trick. O'Ruddy borrows 5 guineas from Jem. Bristol: Earl's valet; parlour with Strepp and Colonel (reconciled). Earl abed: "Straw! Straw! Nothing but straw!" Earl calls O'Ruddy thief/impostor. Lady Mary enters, tends father. O'Ruddy adores her; his scabbard tinkles.

**Ch VI:** Earl raves, foams blood; O'Ruddy: "You yourself stole my papers!" Papers fall from Earl's pillows. O'Ruddy throws sword hilt-first, gives papers to Mary with bow. Strepp: Forister is "my father's partner in the shipping trade," "friend of the family," Mary fond of him. O'Ruddy: "blue-silk ribbon" jibe. Colonel: Forister "one of the finest swordsmen in England." Ponsonby/Stewart duel referenced. Colonel drinks port with O'Ruddy.

**Ch VII:** O'Ruddy considers fleeing; decides to stay. Forister visits: "I shall kill you ten times"; "Nell" (Bristol mistress) and "the child"; O'Ruddy taunts. Colonel enters.

**Ch VIII:** Strepp and Colonel comically bow at door. O'Ruddy in garden; Countess and Mary talk; parrot cries "Pretty lady!" / "Old harridan!"; Countess: "I cannot endure parrots." Mary approaches O'Ruddy: "don't fight with Forister... 'Tis certain death." O'Ruddy: "Am I such a poor stick...?" Mary: "I did not wish you to suppose that I ever failed to pay a debt... Proceed now, sir, in your glowing stupidity."

**Ch IX:** Father's story of Mickey and the lancer. Colonel reveals he was cornet in Earl's regiment, "uncle" to Mary, saw her as a babe in bath. Note "God spare you!" (from Mary, to both men). Duel: O'Ruddy attacks; Forister's left shoulder pierced. Forister flings sword; Strepp pins him.

**Ch X:** O'Ruddy famous; servants flee. Coffee-room: chair dispute; venerable old gentleman. Countess ("Hoity-toity"; "Irish baboon"-type insults). Chair rampart; they revolve round table; Countess throws ivory fan hitting bystander.

**Ch XI:** Forister carried on pallet. Lady Mary and parents leave for London. O'Ruddy rides for Bath; horse lamed in puddle. Overhears Paddy reading letter ("Dear Sister Mary... four shillings you owe on the pig") in haycock: Paddy and Jem robbed the Earl's carriage (purses; Paddy took papers; Lady Mary begged at hood). Gold split in heaps. O'Ruddy: "I forgive you... we will do great deeds."

**Ch XII:** Plans; Jem sent to ride round Bath. Bath inn: Jem described as 8-foot monster. Earl at Bath, drawing-room: O'Ruddy announced as "The O'Rubby." "Papers in the breast of my coat"; sword drawn; "first gentleman who advances is a dead man." Earl: "You have the papers... Why didn't you read the papers?" O'Ruddy: "I would try to get a tutor." Sir Edmund Flixton present.

**Ch XIII:** Earl knows of O'Ruddy's love: "Fool, to match your lies against an ex-minister of the King." Countess in corridor drunk, fights Paddy (she: "Irish baboon"; Paddy: "hell-cat"); servants clean her out.

**Ch XIV:** Countess attacks Paddy in room; Paddy pins her with chair legs; O'Ruddy flees ("Bravo, Paddy!"). Bath → London.

**Ch XV:** Ride; Paddy on Englishmen, Father Corrigan, aunt's burned thatch; "I am knowing the English down to their toes."

**Ch XVI:** Mug-house parlour; Jem bragging ("sticadoro proderodo sliceriscum fencing"; "A blue one"). O'Ruddy trains Paddy and Jem as servants with bottles ("look stupid").

**Ch XVII:** Paddy's hair cut at village; little boys call them Africans. London: river bridge, bustling city, butcher-brewer brawl. Stranger points to "Pig and Turnip," Bishopsgate Street. Landlord; "furrin' gentleman." Mug-house talk.

**Ch XVIII:** Fullbil's club (old wit, wig). Bobbs (dramatist; "I see your nose gradually is turning red"). Fancher (critic; Chinese). Dr Chord (little scientist, kites). Mocked ("Ireland is not in Italy"). O'Ruddy's counter-tale (King of Galway). Flixton recognizes him.

**Ch XIX:** Red Slipper mug-house; Paddy and Jem among footmen; Jem sings ballad by John Snowden about himself. Learned valet quotes "loriot" (bird).

**Ch XX:** Kensington Gardens, Sunday. Chord gossips about society (Marquis of Stubblington, Lord Gram, Banellic girls, Countess Cheer). Lady Mary and Countess appear; Mary looks back.

**Ch XXI:** Father's Mollie-and-the-girl scandal story. O'Ruddy and Mary exchange glances; she looks back; chariot leaves.

**Ch XXII:** Chord claims to be family friend; O'Ruddy announces he'll marry Mary. Earl's town house outside old city gates; small door on oak avenue at back. Chord: Countess drank hot rum (his treatment, 5 yrs ago).

**Ch XXIII:** Plan: climb oak over wall (~10 ft, spikes); Lady Mary walks garden 10 o'clock. Chord's red turban disguise, removed.

**Ch XXIV:** Gardener **Strammers** with blunderbuss ("thief o' the French pears"). O'Ruddy captured, marched through little door. Mary: "Strammers, what would you be doing?" She points blunderbuss; "I'm afraid it's l-l-loaded"; O'Ruddy declares love; Strammers interrupts.

**Ch XXV:** Paddy and Jem befriend Strammers at inn; invited to Sunday gardens. Chord frightened; O'Ruddy: "Gentlemen never murder gardeners."

**Ch XXVI:** Saturday night. Chord warns about papers; suggests giving to Paddy; O'Ruddy suspicious.

**Ch XXVII:** Sunday morning: papers in O'Ruddy's pocket; Paddy and Jem beaten by servants in garden. O'Ruddy enters house via gate; finds Mary locked in boudoir (key outside). Mary: "a door should be locked from the inside." Countess and Earl leave by carriage. Mary advises: papers = "the law"; Temple lawyer **Josiah Brooks**; Brede estate in Sussex; O'Ruddy kisses her. Mary: "I'm a bold man..." She asks about Mass.

**Ch XXVIII:** O'Ruddy in St Patrick's chapel; meets **Father Donovan** (in London, pilgrimage to Rome; **Patsy O'Gorman** died, left £300). Father Donovan to take ship from Rye. Paddy and Jem beaten; O'Ruddy blames Chord. Chord comes, rubbed with liniment; Paddy hits his eye; Jem kicks him; Chord flees ("I shall have the law of us").

**Ch XXIX:** O'Ruddy to Josiah Brooks in Temple: papers "Brede estate"; plan to take possession; Brooks cold. Brooks: possession "nine points of the law." Father Donovan meets O'Ruddy. Night: 9 ruffians ambush O'Ruddy at "Pig and Turnip" (led by captain, "Mr. O'Ruddy... I present you with the spoil"); O'Ruddy disarms all with sword tip, has swords bundled to Brooks.

**Ch XXX:** Brooks returns swords (counted 9). Brooks: 500 guineas from Mary (anonymous). Warns Earl's spies. O'Ruddy orders suits from tailor (pays). Leaves at dawn with Father Donovan; Paddy with bogus packet and papers (Earl's watchers) to ride to Rye by way of London Bridge, Maidstone. Jem with two bundles of swords.

**Ch XXXI:** Ride with Father Donovan. Maidstone road: Paddy beaten by 9 men, papers taken; Jem robs them with black-lined hat mask; saddles piled. Chord among robbers (Jem: "Doctor Chord... fell off his horse"). Jem: "Providence"; Father Donovan troubled.

**Ch XXXII:** Rye; Tom Peel (giant smuggler) hires 9 men (10 guineas each). Father Donovan insists on coming. Brede House: caretaker and wife; O'Ruddy pays 3 guineas; Brede village. Tom Peel: secret tunnel; ghost **Sir Goddard Oxenbridge** (sawn in two). Earl's carriage arrives; O'Ruddy at window; Lord Strepp leads attack; blunderbuss volley; Strepp refuses terms. Night: Strepp's men enter tunnel; O'Ruddy blocks with stones; Strepp comes up as prisoner; they talk ("King O'Ruddy"); Strepp frees men.

**Ch XXXIII:** Paddy falls through trap-door. O'Ruddy and Father Donovan go to Manor House (village Brede). Earl, Countess, Mary, Strepp present. O'Ruddy scatters gold; claims marriage to Mary. Mary: "I can never marry a man I do not love." Countess shakes Mary; O'Ruddy intervenes; Countess slaps O'Ruddy. Mary: "My mother is the danger." Countess brings Mary back consenting; Mary asks Father's blessing. Married by Father Donovan. Memoir ends: children Patrick, Little Mary, Terence, Kathleen, Michael, Bridget, Donovan.

## BOOK 2 of 2: A LITTLE IRISH GIRL (J. M. Callwell, Blackie & Son)

**Chars:** Norah O'Brien (11, short black hair, blue Irish eyes, Irish pride, "Irish" name, mourning frock). Anstace O'Brien (elder sister, governess to Dr Trafford's family, Mrs Trafford). Roderick (eldest, ~21, tall, dark; lawyer's clerk; writer; cough; Dr Trafford treats). Manus (brother, 12, school in Kent under Dr Ford). Piers O'Brien (father, journalist, d. Hampstead, 6 months before, chill). Mother Marion Belthorpe (d. long ago). Lily Allardyce (pink, fair, rich, Hampshire, Heron's Court; goes to Paris). Miss Clarkson (eldest, stately; Treherne House), Miss Susan, Miss Euphemia (junior teacher), Fräulein Glock. Cousin Ansey (Anstace O'Brien, godmother, mad, d. recently, Dublin asylum 12 yrs; lover Hugh Masters never returned). Uncle Nicholas O'Brien (Moyross Abbey, copper mine, Drinane Head; feud with Piers over Marion). Harry Wyndham (grand-nephew, rebellious, banished to Austria/Carpathians). Ella Wyndham (niece, gentle). Miss Browne (governess, "Brownie", Dinapore India). Biddy (Kilshane servant; brother Tom Hogan; Tom's children incl. red-haired Lanty, Bride). Connor (driver). Mr & Mrs Lynch (rector, Cliff church). Captain Charles Lester, R.M. (resident magistrate). Malachy Flanagan (red-bearded still-man/orator). M'Bain (Scotch mine manager). Lady Louisa Butler (Dromore). Cartwright (butler). Dr Hanlon. Pat Lannigan (gamekeeper). Mrs Connor, Thady Connor, pigs.

**Ch I (Treherne House, Hampstead-like N. London):** school for young ladies (Miss Clarksons). Geography: Turkey in Asia. Norah daydreams; "Tuesday fortnight" blunder; sent to bottom of class, must write lesson, not walk. Lily comforts. Background: Piers's death, siblings' struggle; Anstace and Roderick arrange school. Manus in Kent.

**Ch II:** Anstace visits Norah. Legacy: Cousin Ansey's will leaves ~£100/yr property **Kilshane**, near Moyross Abbey, cliffs, Atlantic, to Piers's children. Anstace's story of Uncle Nicholas, Marion's broken engagement, elopement; Nicholas's rebuilt estate. Harry Wyndham to inherit Moyross. Norah: "one of the old O'Briens... a goose." Anstace: Roderick's health; Kilshane outdoor life.

**Ch III:** Norah's song "St. Patrick was a gentleman." Tea-tray toboggan on stairs with Lily; Miss Clarkson catches them, kisses Norah; Norah: "you'd have wanted to toboggan down-stairs too!"

**Ch IV:** Dublin; train to Ballyfin; drizzle; outside-car (driver speaks Irish-English); Kilshane at night. Biddy and Tom welcome: "Begorra... the ould shtock back in Kilshane." Tom carries Norah.

**Ch V:** Kilshane morning: Anstace vs. Biddy's kitchen (hens in kitchen, one-eyed collie, cats, broken Ansey's vegetable dish); Biddy throws candlestick. Anstace: "our mother was an Englishwoman." Attic rooms: Ansey's silver, china, shawls. Biddy: Ansey's history. Lanty leaves fish. Biddy replaced by Bride. Anstace cleans house.

**Ch VI:** Mr & Mrs Lynch; Moyross mine: M'Bain's new machinery, skull-and-crossbones. Manus's letter (diphtheria at school; returns). Norah meets Manus at Ballyfin station. Connor's car. Connor and Mrs Connor's potato scones; sow eats piglets. Runaway pony **Sheila** with **Ella** on Kilshane road; Roderick catches pony. Ella's identity ("Ella Wyndham... Moyross Abbey"). Ella at Kilshane; Miss Browne arrives with bonnet on backwards. Norah invites Ella back.

**Ch VII:** Miss Browne's background (Dinapore cholera; Mrs Wyndham's dying request). Browne suspects O'Briens. Ella at Moyross with Uncle Nicholas; he has portrait of Marion (Ella: Anstace resembles it). He: "not the portrait of any O'Brien."

**Ch VIII:** Seal-hunt: Lanty and Manus plan Ballintaggart Cave; Norah eavesdrops at dairy window, rows to Portkerin; Lanty's coracle; they kill seal with club; Norah stays in recess; Manus fires; seal knocks Manus; Lanty's club.

**Ch IX:** Return by Drinane Head; boat of men; Lanty lands them at Moyross cove; "Monk's Walk." Ghost: white figure; Manus fires — table-cloth hanging on tree (laundry-maid Lanty's sister-in-law? laundry maid cries). Miss Browne scolds laundry-maid and Ella; Manus and Norah keep secret. Lanty left them, going to Drinane Head (secret still).

**Ch X:** Table-cloth scandal; police search. Nicholas closes mine, dismisses men. Roderick forbids Norah seal-hunts. Manus's skull on roof. Lady Louisa's dinner invitation; antique chariot. Captain Lester (R.M.) stays at Kilshane; dinner: Bride's blunders (cauliflower course; "mashed pitaties" in hall). Lester's raid planned at 5 a.m. on still. Manus confides it's Lanty's still on Drinane Head.

**Ch XI:** Norah rises ~3 a.m. (Manus wouldn't wake, refuses); walks alone to Drinane Head at dawn; tarn; hovel; Malachy Flanagan (red beard, red shawl); tells Lanty warning ("Tare an' ages!"). Men sink still; spilled potheen. Lester approaches.

**Ch XII:** Norah hidden under tartan shawl beside Malachy. Lester's search fails. Lester's warning to men. Norah's hat, shawl. Malachy carries Norah on back to edge of moor; Malachy kisses her hand: "one of the raal ould O'Briens." Norah passes Roderick and Lester in road; Anstace's scolding breakfast; Lester says warning was conveyed by "winds." Manus: "you were a pretty gaby."

**Ch XIII:** Anstace and Roderick drive to Dromore (Lady Louisa). Norah and Manus visit mine at dusk; Malachy addresses miners on trolly ("lazy Irish pisants"; Irish pisant; "Nich'las O'Brien"; young Roderick as heir). Crowd heads to Moyross. Norah and Manus run across fields.

**Ch XIV:** Moyross, dinner: Harry (returned without leave, "Carpathian Mountains"), Ella, Miss Browne, butler Cartwright, maids. Norah and Manus at door (Manus: "We've got to see Miss Ella"). Harry bars doors, arms guns. Norah takes quilt and candle; Uncle Nicholas arrives from Dublin via stable-yard, sees Norah ("Who are you, child?"); she takes candle. Norah + Manus exit via pleasure-ground door. Mob at hall-door; Harry threatens. Uncle Nicholas: "Who wants to talk to Nicholas O'Brien?" Norah in abbey high window in white quilt with candle (behind stone). Crowd flees: "the white nun... St. Bridget." Light vanishes; thud.

**Ch XV:** Manus confesses ("It was all Norah's idea"). Harry and Cartwright carry Norah in. Doctor: concussion. Nicholas sends for Dromore by car; Roderick and Anstace return dawn; Nicholas sees Anstace as Marion. Ella nursing Norah.

**Ch XVI:** Nicholas to Roderick: "I'd have welcomed..." Portrait of Marion; "I would gladly give half the little life... that he and I had shaken hands." Harry wants army (Nicholas agrees). Miners' peace; Roderick to manage mine (M'Bain departs). Malachy weeps at door. Lady Louisa visits. Roderick proposes to Ella in Monk's Walk; they'll live at Kilshane; Anstace and Norah at Moyross. Manus to Harrow (planned). Norah wakes early autumn; asks for Lanty; promises Norah he'll stop potheen; Roderick gives Lanty under-keeper post (Pat Lannigan retiring). Anstace knows Lanty's secret. Norah confesses table-cloth. Nicholas: Roderick's heritage unchanged. Norah: "I told you so... Cousin Ansey's... Uncle Nicholas would not leave O'Brien land..." Nicholas: "I wish your father Piers were here." Anstace: year since Piers died. (Text ends mid-conversation.)
